title: Write code top-down
summary: Argues that top-down design—starting with a high-level vision and implementing stubs before working downward into components—produces simpler, more successful systems than bottom-up design, which begins with component details and risks over-generalization and unnecessary complexity.
when-to-read: Read this when deciding how to approach the architecture and implementation strategy for a new system or feature. If you're specifically debating testing strategies or whether to write unit tests first, consult testing articles instead.
